title: Every Sneeze Lands Me by a STRANGER 🤧
premise: In a pollen-gold spring town every sneeze carries you to whoever is thinking about you most; sixty-three sneezes in a row have landed me beside the same old man in a green armchair, with two cups of tea already poured, while my mom has never sneezed once.
twist: The old man is my mom's dad, who has thought about me every day of my life, and Mom takes an allergy pill every morning so she never sneezes and lands next to him; I walk her through the pollen, she sneezes to him, and I sneeze after her.
world: A pastel spring town of drifting gold pollen: a field of tall yellow grass with a path and a bench, a downtown street, an old man's deep-green and cream front room with an armchair, a tea tray and a wall of newspaper clippings, a blue stove in a family kitchen.
